text:
maya: FYI — saw a weird throughput drop on the quant-INT8 runner during the concurrency sweep for model-7B-v2-q. p95 latency jumped ~120ms -> 2.1s for a ~3min window, cost/token briefly doubled. dashboard: https://grafana.company/reports/1768504321

perf-ci-bot: Alert: throughput-drop detected on run 1768504319 (concurrency=64) — p95 jump >5x; traces attached.

sanjay: interesting — looking at runner logs, batch_window_ms jumped and a few shards had batch_size ~124. looks like we accidentally grouped many long prompts together. suspect sample-ordering + shuffle interaction.

eli: i can repro locally with a tiny script. reproduce steps:
```
./harness/run_eval --model model-7B-v2-q --concurrency 64 --shuffle seed=0 --samples 5000
# watch runner_metrics.batch_window_ms and batch_size per shard
```
you'll see windows climb after ~800s and latency spikes.

tasha: quick question — why did the CI report tokens/sec as stable while the harness showed the spike? i pulled both logs and they look contradictory.

maya: good catch. metrics definition mismatch. harness uses successful_tokens / wall_time, CI uses total_tokens / process_time (includes queuing + backpressure). when a batch stalls, CI's denominator shrinks and masks the spike. we should standardize.

sanjay: i opened a small hotfix to runner to: 1) cap batch_size for INT8 models at 64, 2) normalize shuffle ordering to avoid long-run grouping, and 3) add a soft-guard if batch_window_ms > 200 then reduce to 20 and emit a metric. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runner/pull/987

eli: i added a perf-harness contract test that asserts per-shard tokens/sec variance < 30% for a sweep. added as flaky-tolerant but fails loudly if this pattern repeats. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/988

maya: deployed the runner hotfix to staging and re-ran the sweep. no p95 spike on the next two runs, batch_size stayed <= 64, batch_window_ms stable at ~18-22ms.

ops: can we add an alert on the dashboard: if cost_per_token > 2x baseline for 5m then page eng-oncall and attach run_id + trace link? also store raw runner logs for the run in s3.

tasha: i will update CI wiring to enforce metric contract: CI will now fail when tokens/sec definition deviates by >15% between harness and CI instrumentation and will upload raw logs to s3://redwood-perf-raw/<run_id> on failure.

maya: thanks all. next steps: monitor two full sweeps in prod tomorrow morning, then rollback change after 24h if no regressions. tagging @sanjay for follow-up on postmortem snippets. :thumbsup:

perf-ci-bot: deploy started for runner PR 987 -> staging at 1768505170

eli: pushed small log tweak to include run_id in every trace event.

sanjay: will add a short note in the perf-runbook about the ordering/shuffle caveat and the INT8 cap.

maya: good. closing thread once we see two clean prod sweeps.
